summary.title: Tutorial: Make web games with Phaser 3
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a simple browser game in Phaser 3 with scenes, sprites, text, keyboard input, collisions, and tweens.
takeaways: Phaser 3 scenes use preload(), create(), and update() methods, with update() running about 60 times per second.
Sprites and images are loaded in preload() and placed on screen in create(), with arcade physics enabled via this.physics.add.sprite.
Arrow-key input is read with createCursorKeys() and applied to sprite position in update().
Collisions are detected with this.physics.overlap(), and tweens such as scale changes are added with this.tweens.add().
summary.summary: The tutorial walks through building a small coin-collecting game in Phaser 3, a JavaScript framework for HTML5 games. It sets up an index.html file that loads Phaser 3.14.0 from a CDN and a game.js file containing a single scene class. The author then adds a player sprite, a coin, a score text, arrow-key movement, and overlap-based scoring. A final step adds a scale tween when the coin is collected. The page notes that a local web server (for example, python -m http.server) is needed to run the game.
